mac: Apple M1, 8 cores (navigator.hardwareConcurrency 8), 8 GB; Chromium 153 on Metal, WebGPU; a fresh profile; the token to play.maia.city only
how: the loading card looked at every 2 s until gone; a Chromium trace of category toplevel: each thread's top-level tasks, spread over the seconds they span; 'workers busy' = the dedicated workers' task time in a second (so 5.5 = five and a half cores' worth on average); from navigation to the world shown
before_the_pool_workers: job 2's profile of Sandbox 1 (672ae57): ~160 s of worker tasks in its 144 s window, about one worker busy at a time; the page's main thread busy 16 s of it
reading: The pool fills the cores (on average 5.5 and 5.9 workers busy, 138 and 148 seconds with four or more), but the world shows about as late as before (157 s and 173 s against 149-208 s): the workers' total task time rose about sixfold (889 s and 1,024 s against ~160 s), so the same builds take far longer each when they run eight at a time on this Mac (four performance and four efficiency cores, 8 GB), or work is repeated per box. The page's main thread is also far busier (69 s and 82 s against 16 s). Caveat: Sandbox 1's run began with the Mac's load at 13.9 (the quiet wait gave up after 400 s); Sandbox 5's at 3.0.
